description: The Stage 4 review loop applies its git identity to the process environment for the whole run, so every child process it launches inherits the review-loop author. The resolver's pre-push tests then commit with that author and tests that assert the executor identity fail, halting the resolver before push. Apply the review identity only to the git commit the review loop makes, and keep child processes on their own environment.
goal: In the review loop entrypoint, main() stops overlaying the review git identity on os.environ. flow/review/git_identity.py exposes a function that returns a copy of the caller's environment overlaid with REVIEW_GIT_ENV, and the resolver's commit passes that copy to its own git commit only. No test or tool subprocess that the review loop launches sees GIT_AUTHOR_* or GIT_COMMITTER_* values from the review loop, and the review loop still never writes a user section into any git config scope. The module line budgets in holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json are frozen: that file and the budget check scripts must not be edited, and each touched module must stay within its existing budget.
rationale: A per-process identity written into the environment of the whole run leaks into every child process, including the pre-push verification tests, so deterministic test failures stop the resolver before push. Scoping the identity to the one commit keeps the review-loop author on every review commit and leaves the environment of tests and tools unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: In entrypoint/review_loop.py, main() never writes REVIEW_GIT_ENV into os.environ: a test records os.environ at every command the loop runs and finds no GIT_AUTHOR_* or GIT_COMMITTER_* key.

In flow/review/git_identity.py, a function returns a copy of the caller's environment overlaid with REVIEW_GIT_ENV, and the resolver's commit in entrypoint/review_loop.py passes that copy to its one git commit only, so the commit is authored and committed as Holon Review Loop Agent.
A child Python process launched through the review loop's run_cmd during main() sees no GIT_AUTHOR_* or GIT_COMMITTER_* variable; a test in tests/test_review_loop_git_identity.py asserts it.

A commit made through the entrypoint's helpers in a hermetic tmp_path repository with no user.name or user.email configured is authored as Holon Review Loop Agent, and the repository's local and global config still hold no user section afterwards; tests in tests/test_review_loop_git_identity.py assert both.
The review loop entrypoint still runs no git config command that sets user.name or user.email in any scope.
holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json is unchanged, every touched module stays within its budget, and uv run pytest on the changed tests, uv run task lint and uv run task lint-docs pass.
